key_insight: A world model can learn what stays the same while missing what actions change. The paper identifies this failure as “static collapse”: representations retain episode-specific static content but suppress state changes needed for control.
problem_solved: Distributional regularization alone does not guarantee control-relevant representations. Static scene information can be both temporally predictable and diverse across episodes, allowing a model to overlook manipulation dynamics.
method: Study JEPA-style models that predict action-conditioned latent dynamics without reconstructing observations.
Identify static collapse as a failure mode distinct from losing all representational diversity.
The title proposes motion-guided contrastive regularization; the truncated abstract does not provide its implementation or experimental details.
impact: For practitioners, diverse latent representations are not enough: they must also capture action-relevant changes. This motivates evaluating sensitivity to motion and state changes, rather than relying only on distributional regularization.
visual_elements: Two-frame scene: unchanged background highlighted alongside an object moved by an action.
Side-by-side latent diagrams contrasting static collapse with motion-sensitive representations.
Pipeline showing observation encoding, action input, and latent-state prediction.
Conceptual balance graphic: representation diversity versus control-relevant information.
paper_title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
paper_authors: Yiwen Chen, Qiqi Hou, Jisoo Jeong, Yinhao Zhu, Huaizu Jiang
